sections.model_projection: The model projects the Los Angeles Chargers to win at home 25.73 to 19.77, a margin of roughly 6 points, with a projected total of 45.51. The Chargers' win probability sits at 68%. The market currently has Los Angeles favored by 10 points with a total of 47.5, meaning the model's margin is about 4 points softer than the market spread and the model projects roughly 2 fewer total points than the market number. All metrics carry a low-sample flag as this is Week 1 with no 2026 games played, so these figures blend prior-season data.
sections.offensive_matchup: Arizona enters as the league's most pass-heavy offense, running dropbacks on 68% of plays and 66.4% in neutral game scripts (both ranked 1st), but they run into a Chargers defense that ranks 9th in defensive EPA per play (expected points added per play allowed, where negative means the defense is suppressing value) at -0.045 and 6th in defensive success rate at 42.3%. The Cardinals' passing attack generated a modest 0.050 EPA per pass play (17th), and they face a Chargers pass defense that held opponents to -0.040 EPA per pass play (9th). Los Angeles's offense is more balanced but similarly middling in raw production, ranking 19th in offensive EPA per play at -0.005, though their 44.6% third-down conversion rate (4th) suggests they sustain drives effectively. The Chargers' offensive line is a concern, ranking 29th in line yards per rush and 31st in pressure rate allowed, but Arizona's defensive front ranks only 28th in pressure rate generated, limiting how much the Cardinals can exploit that vulnerability.
sections.quarterback_edge: Justin Herbert holds a meaningful career edge over Jacoby Brissett across every major passing metric. Herbert has attempted 2,955 career passes with a 65.9% completion rate, 7.17 yards per attempt, and a career EPA per dropback of +0.053, meaning he adds value on average each time he drops back. Brissett has 1,263 career attempts at 63.7% completion, 6.58 yards per attempt, and a career EPA per dropback of -0.029, indicating he slightly costs his team value on average. The quarterback edge is the single largest individual category contribution to the model's home margin at 0.43 points, reflecting both Herbert's superior efficiency and his significantly larger sample of high-stakes starts (83 games versus 37).
sections.trenches: The defensive front edge is the largest single matchup edge in the model, contributing 0.59 points toward the Chargers. Los Angeles generates sacks on 8.0% of opponent dropbacks (7th) and produces havoc — plays resulting in a tackle for loss, sack, forced fumble, interception, or pass breakup — on 16.6% of defensive snaps (5th). Arizona's offensive line is the most vulnerable unit in this game: the Cardinals rank 30th in line yards per rush (2.53), 24th in sack rate allowed (7.9%), and 26th in pressure rate allowed (24.5%), while also ranking 26th in offensive havoc allowed (16.1%). On the other side, Arizona's defensive front is far less threatening, ranking 28th in pressure rate and 28th in sack rate, which somewhat neutralizes the Chargers' own offensive line issues (ranked 29th in line yards, 31st in pressure rate allowed). The net result is a clear Chargers advantage in the trenches, particularly in their ability to disrupt Brissett.
sections.explosive_play_edge: Both offenses rank near the bottom of the league in explosive play rate — Arizona at 7.2% (28th) and Los Angeles at 7.3% (27th) — so big plays are unlikely to be a decisive factor for either side. The Chargers hold a modest edge because Arizona's defense allows explosive plays on 10.6% of opponent snaps (29th), while Los Angeles allows them on only 8.6% (16th). This means Herbert and the Chargers offense has a better chance of hitting a chunk play than Brissett and Arizona do against the Chargers secondary. The overall explosive edge contributes only 0.06 points to the model, confirming this is a marginal rather than decisive factor.
sections.third_down_red_zone: The Chargers own a significant advantage in both third-down and red-zone efficiency. Los Angeles converts 44.6% of third downs (4th) while holding opponents to just 35.9% (6th); Arizona converts 42.0% (9th) but allows opponents to convert 45.3% (29th), creating a stark mismatch when the Cardinals defense faces third-down situations. In the red zone, the Chargers' defense is the best in the league at preventing touchdowns, allowing opponents to score on only 47.2% of red-zone trips (ranked 1st), while Arizona's defense allows touchdowns on 59.6% of opponent red-zone trips (18th). Arizona's offense scores touchdowns on only 50% of its own red-zone trips (26th), and at 2.63 points per scoring opportunity (25th) they are among the least efficient teams at converting field position into points. The Chargers score on 47.8% of red-zone trips (29th) but generate 2.95 points per scoring opportunity (16th), suggesting they find ways to get points even when they don't reach the end zone.

sections.expected_game_script: Arizona will likely come out throwing early and often — their 68% pass rate and 66.4% neutral-script pass rate are both the highest in the league — but Brissett and the Cardinals offense will face immediate resistance from a Chargers defensive front that generates pressure without needing to blitz (14.2% pressure rate without blitz, 11th). Expect the Chargers to win the line of scrimmage on both sides, limiting Arizona's already-weak rushing attack (ranked 26th in rushing EPA per play at -0.125) and creating enough disruption to force Brissett into difficult third-down situations against a defense that holds opponents to 35.9% third-down conversion. Herbert and the Chargers offense will likely control possession through their superior third-down efficiency (44.6%), though their own offensive line struggles may keep the scoring from becoming lopsided. When Arizona does move the ball into scoring range, the Chargers' elite red-zone defense — the best in the league at preventing touchdowns — should limit the Cardinals to field goals rather than touchdowns, compressing Arizona's scoring ceiling. The Chargers' turnover margin edge (plus-0.17 per game versus Arizona's minus-0.06) adds another layer of risk for the Cardinals if Brissett faces consistent pressure. The overall game script points to a controlled Chargers victory in the low-to-mid 20s, with Arizona staying competitive through volume passing but unable to finish drives at the rate needed to threaten the lead.
